A creator cut with the app on a real 3D phone

a dev-creator reel about the bug that reset every streak in my habit app: show the line of code, the app on a phone, and say sorry. no footage, use the template, vertical.

What the skill did

  • With no footage, it voiced a 6-line script with Chatterbox and drew two cams. Lantern and Sam are made up. 8 shots, 15 s, rendered at 60 fps with motion blur.
  • The code: an editor types the bug on the words (a newline and its indent land as one step), lights the line that resets the streak, punches in, and types the payoff as a status row.
  • The phone is real 3D (Three.js inside the same frame-exact renderer): the proof card flies onto its screen, the camera pushes onto the card, a touch taps Restore, and the toast lifts out toward the lens while the phone defocuses and the days count up.
  • The speaker becomes a post inside a phone, the heart pops on "back", and the camera pushes through the screen into the next shot with the face at the same size.
  • Colours land as drawn: the renderer now writes BT.709-tagged video. Before, browsers played saturated greens up to 39 levels off and shifted the accent.
  • The review: 7 of 7 cuts have a sound, 6 of 6 subs land on a cut, and the final mix transcribes back with no word errors. The second clip is the previous demo, where the product moment was a flat card.

Sound

  • Code: a key tap per typed character, a shine when the line lights, a tick on the status row.
  • The app: the tap clicks about 8 dB under the voice, the toast pops as it lifts and ratchets while its number counts. The heart pops. The push through the phone ends in a reverse riser and a sub boom on the cut.
  • Sub +6 dB over the voice, below 150 Hz only; the bed 12 dB under with 8 dB of ducking. Mastered to -14 LUFS at -1 dBTP.
